meta.description: Queue triage against a standing rule: intake open items, classify urgent/routine/ambiguous verbatim per the rule, notify the owner only when urgent. Read-only end to end.

work_queue.desc: where open items live: a file path, tracker command, or URL

decision_rule.desc: the owner's standing triage rule, applied verbatim

owner_notify.desc: how a human is reached: a command, channel name, or file to write

graph.name: issue-triage
graph.description: THE run_context seed-contract exemplar of the starter set: every seeded value below is a {run.KEY} reference the door binds at launch, and this description IS the key contract a reader (or a `library show` listing) consults before launching. SEED CONTRACT (run_context map, ALL THREE keys required, values plain text - a value containing '{' or '}' breaks re-rendering and the launch refuses; values are persisted into prompts, so put no secrets in them): 'work_queue' = where the open items live (a file path, a tracker command, or a URL your tools can read - intake only reads it); 'decision_rule' = the owner's standing triage rule, quoted verbatim into the classifier; 'owner_notify' = how a human is reached when urgent items exist (a command, a channel name, or a file to write). LAUNCH: run from:'general/issue-triage' run_context:{'work_queue':'...','decision_rule':'...','owner_notify':'...'}. A launch that omits any key (or leaves a ref unbound) refuses BEFORE any write or spawn - that refusal is the contract enforcing itself, not a bug. NODE MAP: intake (enumerate open items) -> classify (apply the rule verbatim; anything the rule does not clearly cover is ambiguous, never forced) -> lap-report (one human touch, only when urgent). ROUTE SEMANTICS: routine items are NOT executed here - this lap only decides; the report names what waits. Every node is read-only toward your tracker.

defaults.context: You are one lane of a queue triage. Ground rules: read-only unless your goal says to notify; the owner's standing rule is applied as written, never improved; every classification cites the field or evidence that drove it; keep the answer to the schema; one fenced json block as the final message; never print secrets.

nodes.goal: Enumerate the OPEN items in the work queue: {run.work_queue}. Read with whatever read-only tools you have; skip items closed or answered out-of-band. Return up to 20 items, each reduced to one line. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"items": [{"id": "<stable identifier>", "summary": "<one line>"}], "count": <int>, "notes": "<anything unreadable or skipped, with reason>"}

Write the triage lap report from classify's committed answer (your Inputs). If - and ONLY if - the urgent bucket is non-empty, deliver exactly ONE notification via the owner's channel: {run.owner_notify}. If that channel is a command, run it once with the urgent list; if a file, append one dated line; if a channel name you cannot reach, set notified:false and say so in report. report = three short sections (urgent / routine / ambiguous-with-questions) that the owner can act from without opening the queue. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"notified": <bool - true only after the notification actually went out>, "urgent_count": <int>, "report": "<the report text>"}
